Verdict: ACCEPT the mathematics and the supplied optimizer. One correction is required to the claimed self-contained checking package.The four substantive claims survive adversarial inspection:The binary-label minimum is exactly the actual-edge expense of TH components.The frontier recurrence, retained-path adapter,  $h+1$  bag bound, and witness reconstruction are correct under the stated conventions.Every full two-row ladder satisfying the selected-neighbour hypothesis has the claimed zero-expense completion, for every  $n\ge 1$ .The cascade has unrestricted optimum  $0$  and retained optimum exactly  $r\mu$ .I found no required mathematical correction and no valid-input correctness defect in the supplied optimizer. My separate execution checks also passed.The required package correction is specific: the attached checker imports check_residual_hall_compensation, whose source is absent from the attachment. Consequently, the attachment does not contain a runnable, fully source-auditable version of its original checker. Include that dependency from the same snapshot, or qualify the self-contained-checker description. This does not invalidate the proofs or the inspected optimizer.1. Exact artifact and evidence boundaryI inspected    source-label-optimizer-audit.txt, containing the proof note, both Python source sections, and the aggregate JSON report.The attachment has:Size: 55,072 bytes.SHA-256: 048ca7feba09b4055f0d10faf457f71625a7fd3b8fbcaa67b6cf21cd96648238.Caller-supplied snapshot identifier: 4a3aa6e1200c428031727813f8ffc8e26e84ec0a.My verdict binds to those attached bytes. I did not independently establish their correspondence with the repository commit.Evidence categoryWhat I actually didProof inspectionInspected the component reduction, retained-path bijection, DP invariant and complexity argument, all- $n$  ladder proof, failure example, and cascade.Source inspectionInspected all of the supplied source_label_dp.py and check_source_label_dp.py.Original-checker executionExtracted the supplied sources and attempted to run the checker. It stopped with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'check_residual_hall_compensation'.Separate executionRan the unchanged supplied optimizer and ladder constructor under Python 3.12.14 using a fresh reference harness with literal matching enumeration and direct alternating-path scoring. Results are detailed below.Supplied reportRead the report. Independently reproduced its ladder totals and all 36 cascade values and work-counter records. I did not reproduce its entire original checking run.The referenced source-label-dp-witnesses.json is also absent from the attachment. I verified witnesses returned during my own executions.2. Binary labels: the exact equality is correctI use the attachment’s notation:  $P$  is the endpoint set of  $M$ ,  $Q=V\setminus P$ ,  $T$  consists of selected white vertices of  $Q$ , and  $W$  consists of the remaining white vertices of  $Q$ .Why every path has exactly one prescribed source labelIn the tagged union  $M+N$ :Every vertex of  $P$  has degree two: one actual edge and one auxiliary edge.Every vertex of  $Q$  has degree one: its auxiliary edge.Thus each component is either a cycle contained in  $P$ , or an alternating path whose endpoints lie in  $Q$ . A path starts and ends with auxiliary edges, so its length is odd. Bipartiteness therefore gives exactly one white endpoint and one black endpoint.This is the decisive use of the white-only source hypothesis. A path cannot contain two different prescribed white- $Q$  source labels that conflict.The local equal-label constraints make the label constant on each component. Consequently:A TH path is forced to label  $1$ .An HH path is forced to label  $0$ .A cycle may have either label.For every feasible labelled pair, therefore,
$$L(N,x)
=
f(N)+
\sum_{\substack{C\text{ a cycle}\\x|_C=1}}
\ \sum_{e\in M\cap C}w_e.$$
Because the weights are nonnegative,
$$L(N,x)\ge f(N).$$
Conversely, for every perfect  $N$ , label its TH paths  $1$  and all other components  $0$ . This is feasible and gives  $L(N,x)=f(N)$ . Hence
$$\min_{(N,x)}L(N,x)=\min_N f(N).$$
For an optimal labelled pair, the stated sandwich is valid:
$$\min_N f(N)\le f(N)\le L(N,x)=\min_N f(N).$$
Thus its reconstructed  $N$  is itself an unrestricted optimum.The adversarial cases are handled correctlyArbitrarily long HH paths. Every actual edge on an HH component has label  $0$ , so every such edge contributes zero. Neither the formulation nor the recurrence imposes a length restriction or charges an HH path merely because it traverses occupied vertices.Common  $M/N$  edges. The two tagged copies form a two-edge cycle. The actual edge is counted once in  $L$ , and the cycle can receive label  $0$ . Treating the overlay as a tagged multigraph is essential; the note does so explicitly.Zero weights. An optimal solution may leave a zero-total-weight cycle at label  $1$ . This creates no discrepancy: its contribution to  $L-f$  is zero. There is no need to force every optimal cycle label to zero.Closed components. They have no source requirement. Their optional label- $1$  charges cannot improve the minimum because all weights are nonnegative.Pointwise equality. The note correctly avoids claiming it for every feasible pair. For example, if  $M=N$  consists of one edge of weight  $1$ , assigning both endpoints label  $1$  gives  $L=1$ , while  $f(N)=0$ . The equality is an optimization statement.Necessity of nonnegativity. With the same common-edge example and weight  $-1$ , label  $1$  gives  $L=-1<f(N)=0$ . The implementation correctly rejects negative weights.I find no missing condition in Theorem 1 as stated.3. Retained paths and frontier DPRetained-path deletion is an exact restriction–extension bijectionFor a retained path
$$v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_{2k+1},$$
the prescribed auxiliary steps are
$$v_0v_1,\ v_2v_3,\ldots,v_{2k}v_{2k+1},$$
and the actual interior steps are
$$v_1v_2,\ v_3v_4,\ldots,v_{2k-1}v_{2k}.$$
The auxiliary steps already match every retained vertex. Therefore a perfect matching retaining them cannot use an auxiliary edge from a retained vertex to the residual board. Every retained interior actual pair is also removed whole, while the endpoints lie in  $Q$ ; hence no actual edge crosses the deletion boundary either.Each retained path removes equal numbers of white and black vertices. The residual board is balanced, and its  $P,Q,T$  are precisely the appropriate restrictions of the original data.Restriction and extension by the fixed auxiliary edges are therefore inverse maps, and expenses add:
$$f_R^*=b_R+f_{\mathrm{res}}^*.$$
This remains correct when the retained paths cannot be jointly extended. Both relevant feasible sets are then empty. No hidden extendibility assumption is needed.The source function prepare enforces the required path conditions: simplicity, disjointness, endpoint membership and orientation, occupied interiors, grid adjacency, and alternating actual pairs. Its fixed labels and fixed expense agree with this proof. Keeping the full original weight dictionary is harmless because the residual DP charges only residual actual edges.The four-state invariant contains all necessary informationAt an event, the state for an active vertex is
$$(x_v,d_v)\in\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\},$$
where  $d_v$  is its current auxiliary degree. In particular, a vertex incident to  $M$  still starts with auxiliary degree zero.For a frontier state, the table stores the least accumulated charge among partial choices satisfying:All source labels already introduced.Every processed actual-edge equality constraint.Every selected auxiliary-edge equality constraint.Auxiliary degree at most one everywhere.Auxiliary degree exactly one at forgotten vertices.Two partial choices with the same frontier state have exactly the same allowable continuations and the same possible additional charges. All future interactions occur through active vertices; every constraint involving a forgotten vertex has already been processed.This is why no connectivity partition is missing. The component argument has reduced source ownership to local label equalities. The matching bit supplies the remaining capacity information.The actual-edge transition is implemented correctlyThe critical detail is that an actual edge imposes its equality constraint and charge whether or not it is selected into  $N$ .The source does exactly this:Unequal endpoint labels reject both alternatives for an actual edge.Its fee is computed once.Both omission and selection alternatives receive that fee.Selection additionally requires two unmatched endpoints and equal labels.This correctly charges actual edges traversed by TH components, rather than charging only edges in  $M\cap N$ .Every grid edge is processed once, at its later-introduced endpoint. A vertex is forgotten only after its last neighbour has been introduced and all corresponding edge events have occurred. These rules establish the stated invariant and the final perfect-matching condition.The  $h+1$  bag bound is validNumber rows  $1,\ldots,h$ , and consider the instant just after introducing row  $r$  of column  $c$ , before forgetting.A surviving vertex of the preceding column  $c-1$  must lie in a row at least  $r$ . A preceding-column vertex in a smaller row has already had its last possible neighbour introduced and has been forgotten. There are at most
$$h-r+1$$
such preceding-column vertices.Current-column vertices occupy at most the first  $r$  rows, contributing at most  $r$ . No earlier column can remain active. Hence
$$|B|\le (h-r+1)+r=h+1.$$
Missing vertices cannot introduce a later neighbour or increase either count. Disconnected and sparse induced boards therefore obey the same bound.Reconstruction and complexity claims are appropriately qualifiedThe source keeps one minimizing predecessor and action per resulting state per event. Keeping an arbitrary predecessor in a tie is sufficient. Backtracking from the final empty state recovers an attaining sequence of label and edge choices, and merging it with the fixed retained data gives a full original witness.There are  $|V|$  introduction events,  $|V|$  forgetting events, and at most  $2|V|$  edge events. Each state has at most two transitions. Thus the claimed bounds hold:
$$O\!\left(|V|\,4^{h+1}\right)$$
state transitions,
$$O\!\left(4^{h+1}\right)$$
rolling state records, and
$$O\!\left(|V|\,4^{h+1}\right)$$
records with full predecessor history.Three qualifications should remain explicit:These are state-record and transition counts. Python tuple construction, hashing, and storage depend on frontier length; integer operations depend on operand bit lengths.Rolling DP memory is not total implementation memory. The implementation also stores  $O(|V|)$  input/preprocessing records such as ordering, neighbours, and expiration information.The shorter-side parameter applies to the appropriate scan. The default scan='auto' chooses that orientation. A manually forced scan uses its own perpendicular bounding-box extent.The note already substantially preserves these qualifications. There is no arbitrary-height polynomial-time claim.The only minor endpoint clarification I would suggest is to state separately that the empty board has optimum zero, since its bounding rectangle is otherwise undefined. The implementation already handles that case correctly.4. The all- $n$  ladder theorem is correctLet  $j$  be bad:
$$w_j\in T,\qquad b_j\in P.$$
Because  $w_j\in Q$ , the actual mate of  $b_j$  cannot be  $w_j$ . In a full ladder it must therefore be  $w_i$  for an adjacent column  $i$ :
$$|i-j|=1,\qquad w_i\in P.$$
Now  $b_j$  is already one occupied neighbour of  $w_j$ . The selected-neighbour hypothesis says there is at most one. Since  $b_i$  is another neighbour of  $w_j$ , it follows that
$$b_i\in Q.$$
The proposed replacement
$$w_i b_j,\qquad w_j b_i$$
uses the two horizontal edges of those adjacent columns. It pairs the selected  $w_j$  directly with black  $Q$ .Why simultaneous swaps cannot conflictThe proof’s disjointness argument is complete:Every bad-column index has its white vertex in  $Q$ .Every mate-column index has its white vertex in  $P$ .Therefore no bad-column index can equal any mate-column index.Two distinct bad columns cannot have the same mate column, because that would give one white vertex two actual mates.Thus the adjacent-column pairs are vertex-disjoint. Their swapped edges, together with all unused rungs, form a perfect matching.Every selected vertex is handled:A selected vertex in a bad column receives the direct black- $Q$  horizontal partner.A selected vertex in a nonbad column cannot be a mate-column white vertex, because those are occupied. Its column remains unused and its rung endpoint lies in  $Q$ .Every TH component is consequently a single auxiliary edge, so its actual-edge expense is zero. Nonnegativity gives optimality.The selected mate edge  $w_i b_j$  belongs to both  $M$  and  $N$ , creating a free tagged two-edge cycle. That feature is consistent with the reduction.The construction also handles boundary columns and  $n=1$ . It uses a linear number of column and matching operations. The source constructor follows this proof accurately.The failure example without the hypothesis is exactFor
$$M=\{w_1b_2,w_2b_3\},\qquad T=\{w_3\},$$
with unit weights, both neighbours of  $w_3$  lie in  $P$ . Therefore any TH path from  $w_3$  must traverse at least one actual edge:
$$f(N)\ge1.$$
For the displayed perfect matching
$$N=\{w_1b_1,w_2b_3,w_3b_2\},$$
the TH path is
$$w_3\xrightarrow{N}b_2
\xrightarrow{M}w_1
\xrightarrow{N}b_1,$$
with expense  $1$ . The common edge  $w_2b_3$  is a free cycle. Hence
$$\boxed{f^*=1}.$$
The violated neighbour count is exactly two. This is a valid counterexample to removing the condition.5. The cascade gives exactly  $0$  versus  $r\mu$ The source uses white vertices of odd coordinate sum, which agrees with all coordinates in the example.Unrestricted completionUnder the all-vertical auxiliary matching, each selected vertex  $(0,4i+3)$  is paired directly with the black- $Q$  vertex  $(1,4i+3)$ .The actual edge in block  $i$  lies instead on the HH path
$$(1,4i+2)\xrightarrow{N}(0,4i+2)
\xrightarrow{M}(0,4i+1)
\xrightarrow{N}(1,4i+1).$$
Its white endpoint is an unselected bottom-row vertex. That actual edge is therefore free.Thus the all-vertical matching has expense zero, and nonnegativity proves
$$f^*=0.$$
Retaining the bottom HH pairsEvery prescribed bottom pair
$$(1,2j)(1,2j+1)$$
is a white-to-black HH path with no actual edge and zero fixed expense.Their deletion leaves precisely the top-row path on  $4r$  vertices. Its perfect matching is unique: the degree-one left endpoint forces its first edge, and repeated deletion forces
$$(0,2j)(0,2j+1)$$
for every  $j$ .In each block the resulting TH path is
$$(0,4i+3)\xrightarrow{N}(0,4i+2)
\xrightarrow{M}(0,4i+1)
\xrightarrow{N}(0,4i),$$
and costs exactly  $\mu$ . These are distinct overlay components, so
$$\boxed{f_R^*=r\mu}.$$
This proves the stated separation for every integer  $r\ge1$  and every  $\mu>0$ .6. height_three_review.scope: Theorem5 feasible all-r 3x6r family, lower bound and full matching
height_three_review.response:
ACCEPT. The construction is feasible for every integer  $r\ge 1$ , and its unrestricted minimum TH expense is exactly
$$\boxed{\min_{N\text{ a full auxiliary matching}} E_{\mathrm{TH}}(N)=r\mu}
\qquad(\mu\ge 0).$$
No mathematical correction is required. The lower bound applies to arbitrary full auxiliary matchings, including those using edges across block joins, and the proposed attaining matching covers every vertex.Here is the audit in detail.1. Block geometry and feasibilityUse the checkerboard colouring implicit in the statement:  $(a,b)$  is black when  $a+b$  is even and white when it is odd. Translation by  $(0,6i)$  preserves both colours and adjacency.Write coordinates locally within a block. The four actual edges are pairwise disjoint and occupy exactly
$$P_i=
\{(0,0),(0,1),(0,2),\ (1,0),(1,2),\ (2,0),(2,1),(2,2)\}.$$
Their translates occupy disjoint vertex sets in different blocks, so their union is an actual matching  $M$  with  $4r$  edges.The white vertices not covered by  $M$  are exactly the five listed in the proof:
$$T_i=\{(0,3),(2,3),(1,4),(0,5),(2,5)\}.$$
All of these are selected. Because they are all white, no two selected vertices are adjacent. Thus, to check the selected-neighbour condition, it suffices to count their neighbours in  $P=V(M)$ .The complete count is:Selected vertex in block  $i$ Neighbours in  $P$  $(0,3)$ Exactly  $(0,2)$  in the same block $(2,3)$ Exactly  $(2,2)$  in the same block $(1,4)$ None $(0,5)$ Exactly  $(0,0)$  in block  $i+1$ , if  $i<r-1$ ; none otherwise $(2,5)$ Exactly  $(2,0)$  in block  $i+1$ , if  $i<r-1$ ; none otherwiseIn global coordinates, the two possible occupied neighbours across a join are
$$(0,6i+6),\qquad (2,6i+6).$$
Consequently, each selected vertex has at most one neighbour in  $P\cup T$ .This explicitly handles the full grid’s interblock edges. At the final right boundary, the possible next-block neighbours are absent, which only reduces the count. The upper and lower boundaries likewise introduce no additional neighbours. Thus feasibility holds for all  $r$ , including  $r=1$ .2. The terminal-path argument is valid for unrestricted matchingsFix any full auxiliary matching  $N$ . Consider the symmetric difference
$$M\triangle N.$$
Every vertex not covered by  $M$  has degree one in this graph, because it has one incident  $N$ -edge and no incident  $M$ -edge. Every vertex covered by  $M$  has degree zero or two, according to whether its  $M$ -edge and  $N$ -edge coincide.It follows that every component containing an unmatched vertex is an alternating path whose endpoints are vertices unmatched by  $M$ . Both its first and last edges belong to  $N$ , so its edge sequence has the form
$$N,M,N,\ldots,M,N.$$
Its length is therefore odd. Since the grid is bipartite, its endpoints have opposite colours.This establishes the precise fact needed in the proof:Every alternating terminal path has exactly one black unmatched endpoint and exactly one white unmatched endpoint.Every white unmatched vertex is selected. Hence every such path is TH; there is no white unselected endpoint that could make it HH.This reasoning does not impose any restriction on where  $N$  runs. In particular, a terminal path may cross several block joins, and the conclusion remains valid.3. The expense lower bound does not double chargeFor each block let
$$b_i=(1,6i+1).$$
This is a black vertex unmatched by  $M$ . Its four neighbours are
$$(0,6i+1),\quad (2,6i+1),\quad
(1,6i),\quad (1,6i+2),$$
and all four belong to  $P$ .Let  $C_i$  be the terminal component containing  $b_i$ . The  $N$ -edge incident to  $b_i$  must therefore enter an occupied vertex  $p\in P$ . At  $p$ , the path must continue along its actual  $M$ -edge. That actual edge cannot coincide with the entering  $N$ -edge, because  $b_i$  is not covered by  $M$ . Thus
$$|M\cap E(C_i)|\ge 1.$$
The components  $C_i$  are distinct. Indeed, each  $b_i$  is a degree-one endpoint, and one terminal path cannot have two black endpoints. Therefore
$$i\ne j\quad\Longrightarrow\quad C_i\ne C_j.$$
Distinct components have disjoint actual-edge sets.Writing the expense explicitly,
$$E_{\mathrm{TH}}(N)
=
\sum_{\substack{C\text{ a TH}\\\text{terminal component}}}
\ \sum_{e\in M\cap E(C)} w(e),$$
we obtain, because every  $w(e)=\mu\ge 0$ ,
$$E_{\mathrm{TH}}(N)
\ge
\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}
\ \sum_{e\in M\cap E(C_i)}\mu
\ge r\mu.$$
This is a component-based lower bound. It does not assume that each component remains inside its centre’s block, or that a component can be assigned a separate expense merely because it visits another block. There are  $r$  distinct TH components, each containing at least one actual edge, and none of those edges is counted twice.4. The explicit auxiliary matching is full and attains the boundAll nine listed auxiliary pairs are grid edges. Their endpoints partition the eighteen vertices of a block as follows:Part of the constructionVertices coveredFirst two auxiliary edges $(0,3),(0,2),(0,1),(1,1)$ Three common  $M/N$ -edges $(0,0),(1,0),(1,2),(2,2),(2,0),(2,1)$ Last four auxiliary edges $(2,3),(1,3),(0,4),(0,5),(1,4),(1,5),(2,4),(2,5)$ These three sets are disjoint and exhaust the block. Thus the nine edges form a perfect matching of that block. Since the blocks have disjoint vertex sets, translating and combining these matchings produces a full auxiliary matching of the entire  $3\times 6r$  grid.Its alternating-component decomposition is exactly as claimed.The one non-direct TH path per blockThe first two auxiliary edges and the first actual edge give
$$(0,3)
\xrightarrow{N}
(0,2)
\xrightarrow{M}
(0,1)
\xrightarrow{N}
(1,1).$$
The first endpoint is selected white, and the second is black unmatched. This TH path contains exactly one actual edge and therefore has expense  $\mu$ .The three common edgesThe edges
$$(0,0)(1,0),\qquad
(1,2)(2,2),\qquad
(2,0)(2,1)$$
belong to both  $M$  and  $N$ . They contribute no TH expense. Equivalently, they disappear from  $M\triangle N$ .The four direct TH pathsThe remaining four edges are
$$(2,3)(1,3),\qquad
(0,4)(0,5),\qquad
(1,4)(1,5),\qquad
(2,4)(2,5).$$
Each joins a selected white vertex to a black unmatched vertex. Each contains no actual edge, so each has expense zero.Neither this  $N$  nor  $M$  uses an edge between blocks. Hence the displayed components remain separate across all joins. The unused edges of the full grid do not connect components of  $M\cup N$ .There is therefore exactly one charged actual edge per block:
$$E_{\mathrm{TH}}(N)=r\mu.$$
Combined with the unrestricted lower bound, this proves the claimed minimum.5. Endpoint cases and the stated consequenceThe argument includes  $\mu=0$ : all expenses are nonnegative, and the displayed matching has expense  $r\mu=0$ . No step requires strict positivity.For unit weights,
$$\min_N E_{\mathrm{TH}}(N)=r,$$
so the minimum expense is unbounded as the length  $6r$  increases while the height remains three.Taking Theorem 4’s height-two zero-expense conclusion as the earlier established input, this proves that its height bound is sharp: the universal guarantee already fails at height three. The family has dimensions  $3\times 6r$ , exactly as stated. The supplemental result establishes the expense formula and that height-sharpness consequence; it supplies no grid-parameter triple-equality claim.Verdict: ACCEPT, with no required corrections. The proof is uniform in  $r$  and uses no finite-test premise.
